entries.block: keeps real mnemonic phrases out of TypeScript test source
entries.reason: A real BIP-39 mnemonic must not appear literally in any TypeScript test source. That is a property of the whole checked-in test set, not of any module's behaviour, so nothing can be executed to demonstrate it. The check walks the source tree and asserts the set of hits is empty. Replace with a secret scanner over the tree if one is adopted.

entries.block: only references legacy mnemonic cleanup in auth cleanup production code
entries.reason: Pins the legacy mnemonic cleanup reference to one production file, so a second call site anywhere under commands/ or infra/vault fails. Which files mention an identifier is a property of the source set; running the code only exercises the call site that exists today. Replace with a static reference check over the built CLI bundle.

entries.block: only writes session memo entries inside SignerSoftwareBase.getHdCredential
entries.reason: Constrains where a decrypted HD credential may be memoized: this is the only check that fails when a new CLI production file starts calling secureCache.set or sessionCache.set. It walks the source set and asserts on what it found, twice - the list of files, then the method that holds the write. Tests that run the code only cover the call sites that exist today, so they cannot see a write added elsewhere. Replace with a static check over the built CLI bundle.

entries.block: does not import axios, secureCache, or getHdCredential
entries.reason: get-address must stay a pure vault read: no network (axios), no session cache write, no seed access (getHdCredential). That is a property of the module's whole reachable graph, not of any one call, so no invocation of the command can demonstrate the absence of those imports. Replace with a static import-graph check over the built CLI bundle, which would also cover transitive reintroduction.

entries.block: %s keeps resource calls JSON-safe without a global codec
entries.reason: On iOS, Android and the extension, main and bg are isolated JS runtimes and hardware resources cross between them as JSON. Reintroducing jpegRgbaUtils or offscreenApiBinaryCodec anywhere on that path breaks the crossing, and absence from a module graph is not observable from any single call. Replace with a static import-graph check over the bg bundle.

entries.block: keeps the adapter SDK out of the runtime import graph
entries.reason: thirdPartyDeviceUtils ships in every platform's main bundle, and a runtime import of @onekeyfe/hwk-trezor-adapter would drag in hwk-trezor-core (~620KB). The parity test in the same file imports that SDK on purpose, so the import graph under test cannot be observed from inside this runtime. Replace with a static import-graph check over the main bundle.

Under Jest every image require() resolves to the one moduleNameMapper stub, so HwWalletAvatarImages cannot tell Pro2Black from Pro2Silver at runtime: only the source says which file each key holds. The byte-compare cases prove the art differs; this pins the wiring so a key aliased onto a sibling art is caught.

entries.block: re-exports the same hooks on web as on native
entries.reason: Web builds resolve hooks/index.web-only.tsx before index.tsx with export presence checks off, so a re-export missing from the web barrel is undefined at runtime (it crashed web Settings). Both barrels import the whole UI layer (Toast, Button, expo modules) and cannot be loaded under Jest, so the test compares their re-export lists. Replace with a web bundle export check if one is added.

entries.block: the named native binding shim preserves data flags and rejects accessors, nonwritable values and Object.prototype
entries.reason: The marker pins the precise inline prelude loop the fixture executes in fresh realms with controlled property descriptors.

entries.block: the named native binding shim preserves data flags and rejects accessors, nonwritable values and Object.prototype
entries.reason: The inline startup prelude has no exported function. The fixture executes its real binding loop in a VM with deliberately constructed property descriptors.

entries.block: actual protected MV3 workers bind inherited native fetch while preserving write propagation and receiver confinement
entries.reason: Pins the one descriptor-lookup mutation used to reproduce the old worker behavior and checks that the comparison left the production prelude untouched.
Checks that the exact request-helper initialization is present once before deriving the comparison fixture. The fixtures execute both versions.

entries.block: Offscreen initializes requests after bridge hardening and retains keep-alive and port recovery
entries.reason: Executes the production Offscreen startup in a VM with browser bridge and timer doubles, including the comparison without request initialization.
Compiles the production Passkey and Offscreen entry variants into a real isolated MV3 extension fixture while substituting its application dependencies.

entries.block: extension global shims install missing aliases before and after lockdown without patching intrinsics
entries.reason: Pins the first import and absence of conflicting polyfills in both isolated bootstrap modules. The VM exercises the shared shim itself under real SES.

entries.block: Web PostHog initializes its shipped SDK with existing privacy configuration and real native history, persistence, and local delivery
entries.reason: Extracts the app’s actual SDK options without loading its production key or starting telemetry. The fixture executes the shipped SDK using those options and a local endpoint.
